key_insight: QFIRE is a positive-security prompt firewall for healthcare AI that blocks out-of-scope and PHI-risk requests, not just obvious prompt injections.
clinical_relevance: It may help reduce unsafe, cross-patient, or privacy-violating LLM outputs in clinical workflows where malicious-looking prompts are not the main risk.
method: Declared natural-language scope constraints to permit only on-task model calls
Asynchronous detector graph with concurrent rules and cheapest checks first
De-obfuscation pass for Base64, hex, ROT13, homoglyphs, leetspeak, and zero-width characters
evidence_signal: In the abstract, QFIRE reports F1 0.86 on 1,968 public injection/jailbreak prompts and introduces QFIRE-HealthBench with 2,000 healthcare prompts including garak and Microsoft PyRIT payloads.
watch_item: Performance claims come from benchmarked detection, so real-world deployment still needs careful tuning for false positives, workflow latency, and safe handling of legitimate PHI-bearing requests.
paper_title: Beyond Injection Detection: A Positive-Security Prompt Firewall that Closes the Scope and PHI Gap SOTA Classifiers Miss in Healthcare
